LITERATURE_LOCKED: classical and scalar complex sequential-growth results
histories Hilbert spaces, vector measures, amplitude processes, and records/decoherence results
Quantum Causal Histories and CP-map evolution
quantum causal-model Markov and d-separation results
TOBC/NTOBC commutative collapse and already-derived CPOBC constraints
REGRESSION_ONLY: extendible scalar Complex Sequential Growth positive control
OPEN_TARGET: finite-dimensional nonsingular noncommutative CPOBC representation in d=3, or an exact no-go explicitly scoped by assumptions/stratum/ansatz
FORMULATION_MISMATCH: Kraus-channel semicausality versus Rideout-Sorkin/CPOBC Bell causality
fixed Quantum Causal Histories versus causet sequential growth
quantum comb/causal box/process causality versus CPOBC
classical covtree dynamics versus operator-valued QSG
quantum causal-model d-separation versus spectator independence

assumptions: Only theorem/definition claims within each source's stated domain are literature-locked.
A later framework is not treated as a solution when its state space, dynamics, causality condition, invertibility assumptions, or event algebra differ from CPOBC QSG.
The absence of a discovered follow-up is a time-bounded literature result, not a mathematical proof of nonexistence.
dimension: The open target is d=3 first and potentially motivated d=4; most locked frameworks are dimension-agnostic or use different dimensions.
field: complex finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces for the open CPOBC target; source-specific fields otherwise
ansatz: The only locked representation failure is the paper's stated d=2 Pauli ansatz; no all-d=2 or d>=3 classification was found.
solver: official arXiv metadata and version histories
exact_numeric_distinction: Bibliography/version/hash facts are exact checks. Literature classification is a conservative interpretive audit. Citation counts and negative follow-up searches are time-bounded.
completeness_scope: All 17 mandatory papers plus targeted follow-up discovery for arXiv:2603.25503.
unresolved_components: No independent proof that the literature indexes used are globally complete.
No searchable text was generated for newly archived PDFs because pypdf was unavailable.
The internal CPOBC relation set and d=3 Jordan strata must be audited by implementation tracks, not inferred from literature absence.

frontier_search.target: higher-dimensional nonsingular noncommutative CPOBC representations, complete classifications, or general no-go theorems following arXiv:2603.25503

queries: "Implementing Bell causality in Quantum Sequential Growth"
routes.result: Official arXiv record only; latest version v1, 2026-03-26; no journal reference or non-arXiv DOI.
The exact Ritesh Srivastava arXiv route returned only arXiv:2603.25503. Sumati Surya's later/nearby arXiv records contained no separate CPOBC representation or no-go follow-up.

The first three arXiv metadata queries returned only arXiv:2603.25503; the broader quantum-sequential-growth query returned 11 records, none a higher-dimensional CPOBC solution. Acronym/narrow synonym routes produced no independent record.
INSPIRE reported 0 citations and no journal/DOI; OpenAlex had no indexed exact-title work; Crossref had no matching publication; Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429.

frontier_search.claim_boundary: The search is sufficient for the repository's mandatory gate but does not establish a theorem that no unindexed or future result exists.

papers.title: Implementing Bell causality in Quantum Sequential Growth
primary_assumptions: non-singular (invertible) transition operators
QSG Markov sum rule and general covariance
operator ordering chosen as TOBC, NTOBC, or precursor-size-dependent CPOBC
antichain transition generators and their induced algebra
established_results: the two natural TOBC/NTOBC orderings collapse the nonsingular transition algebra to a commutative one
CPOBC yields additional commutation constraints without a general commutative-collapse theorem
if an antichain generator lies in the center of the antichain subalgebra, the full transition algebra is commutative
the tested d=2 Pauli representation of the antichain generators is inconsistent
open_or_limited: general form and computability of the CPOBC transition algebra
existence of a higher-dimensional noncommutative representation
the Pauli failure is not an all-d=2 classification and says nothing conclusive about d=3 or d=4
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: No later version, journal record, citing INSPIRE record, or independent exact-title/author/synonym follow-up was found as of 2026-07-28.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: None found. Official version remains v1.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Lock every published relation and collapse result. Research only the mechanically complete finite relation set and an exact higher-dimensional representation or explicitly scoped no-go.

papers.title: A Criterion for Covariance in Complex Sequential Growth Models
primary_assumptions: scalar complex sequential-growth amplitudes
event algebra generated by finite cylinder events
extension assessed through bounded variation of the associated complex measure
established_results: a criterion for extension, hence measurability of covariant events, in the paper's scalar Complex Sequential Growth class
a large family of models satisfying the extension criterion
open_or_limited: not an operator-valued noncommutative transition theorem
not an extension theorem for a Kraus instrument or arbitrary decoherence functional
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Classical and Quantum Gravity 37, 195030 (2020), DOI 10.1088/1361-6382/ab987f; 14 INSPIRE citations at audit. The 2026 QSG paper uses the scalar setting as background but does not replace this extension result.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: No later arXiv version; the peer-reviewed journal version is the publication route.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Use a paper-specified extendible scalar family only as a positive-control regression; do not claim it as a new model or transfer its theorem to noncommutative vector measures.

papers.title: On extending the Quantum Measure
primary_assumptions: strongly positive decoherence functional on an event algebra
associated histories Hilbert space and vector-valued measure
extension to the generated sigma algebra
established_results: the decoherence functional extends if and only if the associated vector measure extends
two explicit non-extension examples, including a causal-set QSG example
open_or_limited: the paper questions whether formal extension conditions may be physically too strong
it does not establish extension for arbitrary noncommutative CPOBC dynamics
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Journal of Physics A 43, 505305 (2010), DOI 10.1088/1751-8113/43/50/505305; 35 INSPIRE citations. arXiv:2003.11311 gives a later criterion in the narrower scalar Complex Sequential Growth setting.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: The later scalar criterion specializes the extension problem; it does not refute the equivalence or counterexamples.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Histories Hilbert space and extension equivalence are prior art; finite-stage checks cannot certify infinite noncommutative extension.

papers.title: A Classical Sequential Growth Dynamics for Causal Sets
primary_assumptions: classical stochastic one-element growth
internal temporality
discrete general covariance
Bell causality and Markov normalization
established_results: derivation of a broad family of classical sequential-growth dynamics
precursor/spectator and Bell-family framework used by later quantum generalizations
open_or_limited: the paper explicitly motivates a future quantum analogue
classical transition ratios do not determine noncommuting operator order
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Physical Review D 61, 024002 (2000), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.61.024002; 246 INSPIRE citations. Covtree papers provide a later manifestly covariant classical route, and arXiv:2603.25503 studies operator-ordering generalizations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Later work generalizes the classical framework and treats zero-probability/manifestly covariant settings; no such result is a noncommutative CPOBC representation.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Reuse conventions and scalar controls; do not report the classical classification as a v0.3.1 discovery.

papers.title: Causal set approach to discrete quantum gravity
primary_assumptions: finite sequential causet growth and path sample spaces
quantum dynamics encoded as a QSGP
amplitude-process and complex-percolation constructions
established_results: a causal-set QSGP framework
an amplitude-process class and a complex-percolation example
finite quantum-measure calculations in the paper's model
open_or_limited: physical viability and continuum/GR interpretation remain prospective
the causality/covariance used is not a classification of nonsingular CPOBC operator algebras
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: No journal/DOI and 0 INSPIRE citations were listed at audit. Gudder's arXiv:1303.0433 and later discrete-QG papers continue the QSGP program.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Later Gudder work reformulates/extends the path-Hilbert-space dynamics; no CPOBC supersede was found.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Amplitude-process ideas are prior art; use neither the model nor its nomenclature as evidence for a new CPOBC representation.

papers.title: A Dynamics for Discrete Quantum Gravity
primary_assumptions: classical sequential growth on the paper's causet class
path Hilbert space
positive operators satisfying normalization and consistency
natural quantum action for amplitude processes
established_results: definition of a QSGP as a Hilbert space with a consistent sequence of positive operators
a concrete amplitude-process realization
open_or_limited: comparison with classical general relativity is speculative
the construction does not impose the 2026 paper's CPOBC operator relations
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in International Journal of Theoretical Physics 53, 3575-3586 (2014), DOI 10.1007/s10773-013-1940-5; 2 INSPIRE citations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: The arXiv record notes text overlap with arXiv:1108.2296; this is a provenance warning, not a refutation of the mathematical definitions.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Histories/amplitude construction is locked prior art and is not a substitute for CPOBC representation search.

papers.title: Somewhere in the Universe: Where is the Information Stored When Histories Decohere?
primary_assumptions: decoherent-histories framework
pure or mixed initial states
environmental records and coarse graining
established_results: extension of the histories-record connection to mixed states with imperfect records
explicit one-bit-environment and quantum-Brownian-motion analyses
open_or_limited: the broad information-count relation is presented as a conjecture and checked in specified models
records suppress rather than generate history interference
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Physical Review D 60, 105031 (1999), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.60.105031; 105 INSPIRE citations. Later records/decoherence work refines the framework.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: No correction relevant to the narrow orthogonal-record boundary was found.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Orthogonal records causing decoherence are a regression baseline, never a novel coherent-geometry construction.

papers.title: Strong Decoherence
primary_assumptions: pure initial state
homogeneous, possibly branch-dependent chains of projections
generalized records and approximate permanence conditions
established_results: strong decoherence implies probability consistency
strong decoherence is strictly stronger than consistency or medium decoherence
record conditions ensure permanence of the past under history extension
open_or_limited: the conditions are an idealization and not a sequential-growth Bell condition
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in conference proceedings (1998), with no DOI listed; 51 INSPIRE citations. Gell-Mann and Hartle's arXiv:1312.7454 later revisits strong decoherence in quasiclassical realms.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Later work adapts/refines strong decoherence; no result equates it to CPOBC.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Use only as a records/decoherence boundary, not as Bell-causal quantum geometry.

papers.title: Quantum causal histories
primary_assumptions: a causal set with a Hilbert space attached to each event
local unitary evolution operators
quantum analogues of reflexivity, antisymmetry, and transitivity
established_results: definition of Quantum Causal Histories
directed topological-quantum-field-theory interpretation when transitivity holds
open_or_limited: fixed causal structure with local quantum systems is not sequential growth of the geometry
its causality axioms are not Rideout-Sorkin Bell causality
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Classical and Quantum Gravity 17, 2059-2072 (2000), DOI 10.1088/0264-9381/17/10/302; 88 INSPIRE citations. arXiv:hep-th/0302111 is the direct formal refinement.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: The 2003 refinement replaces the early local-unitary presentation with event algebras and CP maps under explicit extension axioms.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Do not reimplement Quantum Causal Histories or relabel their causality as CPOBC.

papers.title: Evolution in Quantum Causal Histories
primary_assumptions: discrete locally finite causal pre-spacetime
matrix algebras at events
completely positive maps along causal relations
extension and commutativity conditions for spacelike/complete pairs
established_results: a precise local-algebraic QCH definition
local CP evolution suffices and unitary evolution is recovered where expected
open_or_limited: the causal graph is supplied rather than generated
CP consistency is not CPOBC spectator independence
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Classical and Quantum Gravity 20, 3839 (2003), DOI 10.1088/0264-9381/20/16/320; 46 INSPIRE citations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Refines arXiv:hep-th/9904009; no equivalence with sequential-growth Bell causality was found.
papers.boundary_for_v031: QCH CP maps are cited prior art; the Kraus/channel track remains a separate formulation.

papers.title: Causal and localizable quantum operations
primary_assumptions: fixed bipartite or multipartite quantum systems
completely positive superoperators
relativistic no-signalling and implementation-resource definitions
established_results: causal operations need not be localizable
a semicausality criterion
semicausal complete-measurement superoperators are semilocalizable
open_or_limited: the initial paper leaves the all-operation semicausal-to-semilocalizable statement as a conjecture
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Physical Review A 64, 052309 (2001), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.64.052309; 210 INSPIRE citations. arXiv:quant-ph/0104027 proves the general conjecture.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Eggeling-Schlingemann-Werner generalizes the semilocalizable result from the restricted class to arbitrary semicausal operations.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Channel no-signalling theory is locked but does not define CPOBC.

papers.title: Semicausal operations are semilocalizable
primary_assumptions: bipartite completely positive maps
one-way no-signalling
Stinespring representation and its uniqueness
established_results: every semicausal operation is semilocalizable
open_or_limited: transfer to relativistic quantum field theory is only sketched as problematic
the theorem concerns fixed-party signalling, not causet spectators
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Europhysics Letters 57, 782-788 (2002), DOI 10.1209/epl/i2002-00579-4; 106 INSPIRE citations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Proves and strengthens the conjecture left in arXiv:quant-ph/0102043; no CPOBC implication follows.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Do not reprove semicausal/semilocalizable channel theory or use it as a Bell-causality certificate.

papers.title: Theoretical framework for quantum networks
primary_assumptions: quantum networks represented by Choi operators
typed input/output systems
link product and recursive normalization of deterministic combs
established_results: quantum-comb framework for networks and transformations of networks
universality of memory channels for admissible quantum-network transformations
open_or_limited: the paper asks whether universality can fail in nonquantum theories
comb normalization is not causal-set MSR/GC/CPOBC
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Physical Review A 80, 022339 (2009), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.80.022339; 585 INSPIRE citations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Extensively generalized by later higher-order/process-tensor literature; no result found identifies comb causality with CPOBC.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Quantum comb/process-tensor ideas are prior art and outside the main CPOBC line.

papers.title: Causal Boxes: Quantum Information-Processing Systems Closed under Composition
primary_assumptions: messages indexed by positions in a partially ordered set
Fock-space input/output wires
a causality function controlling finite-cut behavior
closure under parallel and loop composition
established_results: definition of causal boxes
closure under composition
support for superposed message order and composable protocol analysis
open_or_limited: systems process messages on a supplied position set rather than grow causal-set geometry
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 63, 3277-3305 (2017), DOI 10.1109/TIT.2017.2676805; 69 INSPIRE citations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: The official arXiv history says v2 weakened the causality definition; v3 made minor referee edits and matches the published version up to layout.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Causal-box composition and QSG Bell causality remain different formulations.

papers.title: A manifestly covariant framework for causal set dynamics
primary_assumptions: covtree nodes are sets of finite unlabeled causal sets
classical random walks on covtree
stem-generated event sigma algebra
established_results: every infinite covtree path corresponds to at least one infinite unlabeled causal set
transition probabilities induce a classical measure on the stem sigma algebra
open_or_limited: does not provide a quantum covtree dynamics
does not impose CPOBC transition-operator relations
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Classical and Quantum Gravity 37, 085003 (2020), DOI 10.1088/1361-6382/ab719c; 12 INSPIRE citations. arXiv:2008.02607 is a direct structural follow-up.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: The structural follow-up studies paths, self-similarity, breaks, posts, and renormalisation without quantizing covtree.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Classical covtree is locked and is not to be reimplemented or quantized in this version.

papers.title: The structure of covtree: searching for manifestly covariant causal set dynamics
primary_assumptions: the covtree partial order and its path-to-infinite-causet correspondence
classical transition probabilities
established_results: identification of paths corresponding to posts and breaks
covtree self-similarity and a cosmic-renormalisation-like transformation
classification of paths for causets with unique natural labeling
open_or_limited: selecting physically motivated covtree dynamics remains open
quantum/noncommutative covtree dynamics is not constructed
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: Published in Classical and Quantum Gravity 38, 015001 (2021), DOI 10.1088/1361-6382/abc135; 8 INSPIRE citations.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: Extends the 2019 covtree framework structurally; no CPOBC representation result was found.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Covtree structure is prior art, not the v0.3.1 open target.

papers.title: Quantum Causal Models
primary_assumptions: quantum processes associated with directed acyclic causal graphs
unitary circuit dilations and marginalization over local noise
intrinsic quantum conditional-independence notion
established_results: unitary circuits have DAG causal structures
a quantum Markov condition and converse
soundness and completeness of d-separation for the paper's quantum conditional independence
quantum analogues of do-calculus rules
open_or_limited: the arXiv paper is not listed with a journal publication
process causal models do not encode sequential causet births or CPOBC spectators
papers.follow_up_and_citation_audit: No journal/DOI listed for this preprint; 126 INSPIRE citations. arXiv:2002.12157, published as Nature Communications 12, 885 (2021), extends the framework to cyclic quantum causal models.
papers.corrections_modifications_generalization: v2 significantly expanded the introduction/discussion and rewrote Section 4; cyclic quantum causal models are a substantive generalization, not a CPOBC solution.
papers.boundary_for_v031: Causal-model Markov/d-separation results are cited background only.
